sites.note: Uses Gaia's own precomputed best-neighbour table rather than a positional match of ours, so the epoch handling is the Gaia consortium's and is correct by construction.

The main sample's infrared photometry is joined through gaiadr3.allwise_best_neighbour and the 2MASS best-neighbour table inside ADQL. These are the consortium cross-matches, which propagate properly. No channel downstream of the main sample -- Search B, Search U among them -- is exposed to this bug at all.

summary: 0 site(s) materially damaged, 2 carrying the omission without measurable damage. The two sites that skip epoch propagation, Search C and Search L, are matching samples whose proper motions are small against their match radii. Search C is measured directly: the 21-year NVSS baseline moves the median star 0.5" against a 5" radius and carries 0.12% of the sample past it. Search L's cached sample no longer holds proper motions, so it is judged on what its match actually achieved -- 99.0% of sources matched, 99% of separations inside 1.41" of a 3" radius -- which is not the signature of an epoch drift reaching the radius. Neither null is affected. The omission remains a live hazard, because the same code applied to a nearby or high-proper-motion sample is exactly what produced the fake null in the nearest-10-pc channel, and nothing in either script prevents that reuse.
